title: Keep the scene. Send the changes.
idea: Scrub a synthetic 3D set beside its cached approximation. Compare a position-only ranking with position-and-color ranking; watch a stationary surface go stale.
controls: Update budget, frame-group length, time, ranking, color-change toggle, orbit; one-click PNG/GIF in square or wide format.
misconception: Stationary means unchanged, or caching a splat removes its rendering cost.
connection: ResStreamGS · 15 Oct 2026. Implemented analytic scene. Known synthetic trajectories rank updates; not its learned probe, training, codec or mobile benchmark. Record counts are not compressed bytes.
recommendation: Existing weekly kit remains ready; retained while new topics await implementation.

title: Freeze time. Move the camera.
idea: A colored Gaussian scene with fixed background splats and moving foreground splats; separate panels reveal static aggregation and dynamic interpolation.
controls: Independent time and camera-orbit sliders; Static/dynamic probability threshold; Velocity-arrow display; Interpolation amount and occlusion overlay; planned PNG/GIF export in light, minimal theme.
misconception: A plausible generated video already contains an explicit, reusable 4D scene.
connection: SplatFlux · 20 Oct 2026. A shared decoder converts observed or generated video latents into 4D Gaussians, separating static structure from moving primitives. Motion interpolation supports changing time and viewpoint without rerunning a network at each timestamp. Synthetic analytic Gaussian demonstration, not SplatFlux inference or recovered geometry.
recommendation: Best new research-to-visual pairing: static/dynamic representation and independent time/camera controls. Proposed, not implemented.

title: The edit happened — but did it stay?
idea: A small animated scene with requested-state, observed-state and preservation lanes, highlighting missed, delayed and reverted changes.
controls: Move instruction arrivals along a timeline; Choose target object and requested appearance; Adjust response lag and retention failure; Toggle visual quality versus edit success; planned PNG/GIF export in light, minimal theme.
misconception: High visual quality implies instruction compliance.
connection: StreamEval · 20 Oct 2026. New benchmark for evolving instructions and preservation during streaming video, beyond scoring completed clips. Analytic state-machine teaching demo, not a StreamEval run or model output.
audience: Creative video practitioners and ML engineers
recommendation: Useful counterpart to vendor demos: execution and preservation are separate.

title: A wall needs fewer splats than leaves
idea: Render a synthetic scene containing broad flat regions and fine details, compare which colored ellipses survive truncation, and plot error against budget.
controls: Gaussian budget from 0.1% to 100%; Opacity-only versus complexity-aware ranking; Complexity heatmap; Bandwidth and current transfer time; planned PNG/GIF export in light, minimal theme.
misconception: Keep the most opaque Gaussians and every region degrades fairly.
connection: KoalaGS · 20 Oct 2026. Complexity-aware allocation and importance ordering keep a single trained Gaussian scene useful when only a prefix of its primitives is rendered. Analytic ranking demonstration; not trained KoalaGS, not its measured quality curve.
recommendation: A budget/error lesson that extends the existing scene-streaming lab.

title: Generating pieces does not mean receiving them early
idea: Separate audio generation, decoding, buffering and playback on colored lanes. Contrast Phonon’s 80 ms latent frames with application buffering and Ming’s documented whole-waveform response.
controls: Latent steps, decode chunk size, buffer policy, waveform length and first-playable-sample marker; planned PNG/GIF.
misconception: A streaming HTTP flag guarantees incremental speech playback or exposes every model task.
connection: Phonon v0.4.0 runtime · 20 Oct 13:36 UTC; Eleven Realtime announcements · 20/21 Oct; Ming serving limitation retained. Compare incremental latent generation, waveform decoding, transport and playback. Proposed analytic timeline, not measured latency.

title: Two velocities, two very different meanings
idea: Advect colored smoke through a numerical 2D fluid field beside a separate latent sampling trajectory. Show what changes when a visual-quality reward favors appearance over reconstruction.
controls: Curl, divergence, viscosity, time step, density injection, vector/color encoding and reward weights; planned PNG/GIF.
misconception: A flow-matching velocity is the physical velocity of smoke, or a physics-inspired reward enforces Navier–Stokes.
connection: FluidGen · 19 Oct 2026 UTC. Proposed numerical teaching model; no FluidGen inference or reproduction.
recommendation: Retained deep fluid-dynamics proposal; no new FluidGen release found.

title: An empty first frame cannot show the effect
idea: Scrub a transparent-visible-transparent effect and shift the visible reference to the conditioning boundary before restoring the original phase.
controls: Visible reference, phase offset, alpha ramp, timeline and checkerboard/colored background; planned PNG/GIF.
misconception: A transparent starting frame provides an appearance reference, or a four-step text-video result applies to image-conditioned sampling.
connection: Wan-Alpha++ · paper 19 Oct; availability corrected 23 Oct. Ordinary RGBA I2V adapters/code are public; specialized effect weights remain pending. Proposed analytic alpha/phase/compositing lab, not model inference.

title: The same rectangle can face two different ways
idea: Stage colored 3D actor boxes, switch among three cameras and inspect projected coordinate-color maps plus global/shot/subject attention masks.
controls: Actor position, yaw, camera pose, shot boundary and attention scope; planned PNG/GIF.
misconception: A 2D box specifies orientation, or identity consistency in one generated sequence guarantees identity across separate edits.
connection: Mise-en-Video · 19 Oct 2026. Proposed analytic projection/attention illustration, not generated footage.
